title: Affine perfect extension after adjoining a finite locally free summand
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U a quasi-compact open subscheme of X. For every perfect object F of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex], there exist an integer r and a finite locally free \mathcal O_U-module \mathcal F such that \mathcal F[-r] \oplus F is isomorphic on U to the restriction of a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X).

proof.text: By perfectness and [lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor], F is pseudo-coherent and each point of U has a neighbourhood with a finite Tor-amplitude interval. Since U is quasi-compact, choose a finite such cover and take the minimum of its lower bounds and the maximum of its upper bounds; locality of derived tensor products then gives one interval [a,b] valid on all of U. Apply [lem-sc-affine-pseudo-coherent-lift] to obtain a bounded-above complex P^\bullet of finite free \mathcal O_X-modules whose restriction represents F.

source.place: Tag 08ED proof, first paragraph: pseudo-coherence and Lemma 08EE

proof.text: Choose r below the lower Tor-amplitude bound a. Put K = Im(P^{r-1} \to P^r); since H^i(F)=0 for i<a, on U the sheaf \widetilde K|_U is the kernel of \widetilde{P^r}|_U \to \widetilde{P^{r+1}}|_U. The truncation-kernel statement [lem-sc-affine-truncation-kernel-finite-locally-free] gives that \widetilde K|_U is finite locally free. The complex Q=(\widetilde K|_U \to \widetilde{P^r}|_U \to \widetilde{P^{r+1}}|_U \to ...), with \widetilde K|_U in degree r-1, is strictly perfect and represents F, while P=(P^r \to P^{r+1} \to ...) is bounded, finite free, and hence perfect on X. The stupid truncation \sigma_{\ge r}Q=P|_U gives a distinguished triangle P|_U \to F \to (\widetilde K|_U)[1-r] \to (P|_U)[1] (Stacks prints the shift as [-r-1]; with \widetilde K|_U in degree r-1 the correct shift is [1-r]).

source.place: Tag 08ED proof, truncation at r and the displayed distinguished triangle

proof.text: By [lem-sc-perfect-ext-bounded-qcoh-vanishing] applied on the quasi-compact separated scheme U to the perfect object F, there are integers a'\le b' such that Hom(F,L)=0 for every L in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_U) with H^i(L)=0 for i in [a',b']. The object (\widetilde K|_U)[1-r] is a quasi-coherent sheaf placed in degree r-1, so choosing r with r-1<a' (in addition to r<a) gives Hom(F,(\widetilde K|_U)[1-r])=0. Thus the connecting map F \to (\widetilde K|_U)[1-r] in the triangle is zero.

source.place: Tag 08ED proof, final sentence invoking Lemma 09M4

proof.text: A distinguished triangle A\to B\to C\to A[1] whose map B\to C is zero splits: A\cong B\oplus C[-1] (the split-triangle lemma, Stacks Derived Categories, Lemma derived-lemma-split). Hence P|_U \cong (\widetilde K|_U)[-r] \oplus F. Therefore the perfect object P of D(\mathcal O_X) restricts to \mathcal F[-r]\oplus F with \mathcal F=\widetilde K|_U finite locally free, which is the assertion with this r (Stacks writes [-r-2] here, an inherited shift typo; the conclusion is existential in r).

source.place: Tag 08ED proof, final sentence: apply Derived Categories, Lemma 4.11 (split triangle)
